subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust signal for generated HTML after outbound media staging?
rationale: The patch appears technically sound, but it intentionally broadens a local host-read HTML security boundary and that acceptance is a maintainer/security policy choice rather than an automated repair decision.

options.title: Accept provenance lifecycle
options.body: Merge the PR with the current content-bound sha256/size provenance, read-once verification, and cleanup behavior as the approved trust lifecycle.

options.title: Require tighter lifecycle first
options.body: Ask the contributor to add a bounded row TTL, chunked cleanup, or another explicit lifecycle guard before merge.

options.title: Reject outbound HTML trust expansion
options.body: Keep staged outbound HTML blocked and require a different product path such as converting generated HTML to another deliverable format before Telegram delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance lifecycle
recommendation.body: Merge the PR with the current content-bound sha256/size provenance, read-once verification, and cleanup behavior as the approved trust lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current trusted generated-HTML host-read seam that this PR extends, and the PR discussion already routes the security-boundary decision to them.
